55 engagements

Banks and investors can assess a financing when the structure, the model and the Shariah contract arrive as one pack.

Banking, capital markets and Sukuk account for 55 of the 650+ engagements in HAYKALAH’s archive census, 2004–2026. Through FINA., its financial structuring practice, HAYKALAH designs Sukuk, funds and facilities, runs bank processes from the borrower side and prepares the models and documents that lenders and investors rely on. Each structure is approved by a Shariah board, and regulated activities are executed through appropriately licensed partners.

Archive census counts are indicative.

What we do

  • Sukuk structures based on Ijara, Istisna’a, Musataha and Wakala.

  • Bank processes: the banking document, the request for offers and a like-for-like comparison of terms.

  • Fund structures and term sheets, with each fund set up and managed by a CMA-authorised manager.

  • Asset-backed securitization and off-balance-sheet vehicles.

  • Readiness for Sukuk and tokenization: proofing checklists, data rooms and screening bands.

  • Financial models of record and information memoranda.

  • Governance roles on fund boards.

How we create value

  • 01

    Innovation

    For stadium precincts, HAYKALAH proposed a Sukuk framework of Musataha, Istisna’a and Ijara with one issuer per stadium (proposal, no mandate).

  • 03

    Optimization

    For a Holy Sites master developer, HAYKALAH compared offers from five banks on limit, tenor, margin and conditions and recommended one facility for over SAR 1bn of works (2022).

  • 04

    Automation

    For three income-producing assets in Riyadh, a 34-point proofing checklist and a data-room design keep the documents investors review in one place (2025).

Questions

What are screening bands?

Thresholds an asset’s cash flows must meet before a structure is chosen. For three income-producing assets in Riyadh in 2025, they were occupancy above 85% and debt-service cover of at least 1.20x.

Who issues the Sukuk that HAYKALAH structures?

The issuer, usually through an SPV that holds the asset for the Sukuk holders. HAYKALAH structures, models, documents and coordinates. It does not issue, offer or deal in securities; those steps are carried out by a CMA-authorised institution engaged for the transaction.

Who approves the structure under Shariah?

The Shariah board of the issuer, fund or financial institution involved. Where a client has none, HAYKALAH can arrange an independent Shariah board for the transaction.
